##### Critical Values of the Chi-Square Distribution {#sec-eda-chi-square-distribution-table}

This table contains the critical values of the [chi-square distribution](#sec-eda-chi-square-distribution). Because of the lack of symmetry of the chi-square distribution, separate tables are provided for the upper and lower tails of the distribution.

A test statistic with $\nu$ degrees of freedom is computed from the data. For upper-tail one-sided tests, the test statistic is compared with a value from the table of upper-tail critical values. For two-sided tests, the test statistic is compared with values from both the table for the upper-tail critical values and the table for the lower-tail critical values.

The significance level, $\alpha$, is demonstrated with the graph below which shows a chi-square distribution with 3 degrees of freedom for a two-sided test at significance level $\alpha = 0.05$. If the test statistic is greater than the upper-tail critical value or less than the lower-tail critical value, we reject the null hypothesis. Specific instructions are given below.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-chi-square-distribution-table-shaded
#| fig-cap: "Two-sided test for alpha = 0.05 (chi-square distribution, 3 df)"
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

df <- 3
upper_crit <- qchisq(0.975, df)
lower_crit <- qchisq(0.025, df)

tibble(x = seq(0.001, 12, length.out = 401)) |>
  mutate(y = dchisq(x, df)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = ~ filter(.x, x >= upper_crit),
    aes(ymin = 0, ymax = y),
    fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = ~ filter(.x, x <= lower_crit),
    aes(ymin = 0, ymax = y),
    fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  labs(x = "x", y = "f(x)") +
  theme_light()
```

Given a specified value of $\alpha$:

1. For a two-sided test, find the column corresponding to $1 - \alpha/2$ in the table for upper-tail critical values and reject the null hypothesis if the test statistic is greater than the tabled value. Similarly, find the column corresponding to $\alpha/2$ in the table for lower-tail critical values and reject the null hypothesis if the test statistic is less than the tabled value.
2. For an upper-tail one-sided test, find the column corresponding to $1 - \alpha$ in the table containing upper-tail critical values and reject the null hypothesis if the test statistic is greater than the tabled value.
3. For a lower-tail one-sided test, find the column corresponding to $\alpha$ in the lower-tail critical values table and reject the null hypothesis if the computed test statistic is less than the tabled value.

**Upper-tail critical values of chi-square distribution with $\nu$ degrees of freedom**

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: tbl-chi-square-distribution-upper
p_upper <- c(0.90, 0.95, 0.975, 0.99, 0.999)

crossing(nu = 1:100, p = p_upper) |>
  mutate(x = qchisq(p, df = nu)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = p, values_from = x, names_prefix = "p") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("nu", as.character(p_upper)))
```

**Lower-tail critical values of chi-square distribution with $\nu$ degrees of freedom**

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: tbl-chi-square-distribution-lower
p_lower <- c(0.10, 0.05, 0.025, 0.01, 0.001)

crossing(nu = 1:100, p = p_lower) |>
  mutate(x = qchisq(p, df = nu)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = p, values_from = x, names_prefix = "p") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("nu", as.character(p_lower)))
```
